title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — July 2026
description: Out of 17 IPOs reviewed, 10 are currently trading above their original issue price. 7 companies are currently trading below their original issue price.

faq.a: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise money, allowing ordinary people to buy a part of the company.
An SME IPO is an IPO by a Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) that lists on a separate platform of the exchange (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME) with different rules compared to mainboard IPOs.
The "issue price" is the fixed price per share at which a company offers its shares to investors during an IPO.
The "listing price" is the price at which a company's shares start trading on the stock exchange on its first day.

faq.q: What does "return vs. issue price" mean?
faq.a: This figure tells you the percentage difference between the current market price of a share and its original IPO (issue) price. A positive percentage means the share is trading above its IPO price, while a negative percentage means it's below.
